note: Live Jupiter answers for 10 USDC -> MEW and the MEW back to USDC, built for the same throwaway public key as jupiter-usdc-popcat-swap.json (its secret was never kept). MEW has no direct USDC pool (onlyDirectRoutes answered NO_ROUTES_FOUND the same morning: jupiter-cat-route-shapes.json), so the quotes were asked the way src/lib/jupiter-swap.mjs asks for one hop through SOL: onlyDirectRoutes=false, restrictIntermediateTokens=true, maxAccounts=24, instructionVersion=V2, 100 bps (the exact queries are under `query`); the transactions the way it builds a hop: useSharedAccounts true, no SOL wrapping, dynamicComputeUnitLimit false, a 50,000-lamport priority cap. The lookup tables, and every account the three transactions name writable, are this RPC's read at slot accountsSlot (writableAccounts). The buy quote's priceImpactPct was 0 and the sell's 0.0067 (0.67%), both inside the agent's caps. WHAT THE BYTES SHOW. Each quote is two hops at 10000 bps each: USDC -> SOL on one pool and SOL -> MEW on another (the sell the reverse). Each shared transaction is a compute-unit limit, a compute-unit price, one idempotent account create (the wallet's MEW account on the buy, its USDC account on the sell) and one shared_accounts_route_v2 (discriminator d19853937cfed8e9). Its data: the discriminator; one byte naming which of Jupiter's eight program authorities runs the route (7 on the buy, 3 on the sell; each is the PDA of the seeds "authority" and that byte under the Jupiter program); in_amount, quoted_out, slippage, platform fee and positive slippage at fixed offsets; then the route plan, a u32 count (2) and per step a Swap enum (one variant byte and a payload whose length depends on the AMM: none for 1DEX and Raydium, nine bytes for Flux), bps u16, input index u8, output index u8. Step one goes index 0 -> 1 and step two 1 -> 2: 0 is the input mint, 1 the SOL, 2 the output mint. Because the payloads differ, the steps cannot be read from the front without a table of every AMM Jupiter routes, but the route plan is the instruction's last argument, so its last four bytes are always the last step's bps and indexes (10 27 01 02 in all four). Accounts: [0] the program authority, [1] the wallet (the only signer), [2] the wallet's input account, [3] and [4] the program authority's own associated accounts for the input and output mints, [5] the wallet's output account, [6] and [7] the two mints, [8] and [9] their token programs, [10] the event authority, [11] Jupiter; then each AMM's accounts. WHERE THE INTERMEDIATE SOL LIVES: in the program authority's own wrapped-SOL associated account (BuqEDKUwyAotZuK37V4JYEykZVKY8qo1zKbpfU9gkJMo for authority 7 on the buy, 7x4VcEX8aLd3kFsNWULTp1qFgVtDwyWSxpTGQkoMM6XX for authority 3 on the sell), written by both steps and owned by the authority, not the wallet. The wallet's own wrapped-SOL account (BNAQv1Ryy3ADTj1WvWVxSsPfsU6RKJxVn65hyLEyhjHS) is named by neither transaction; the only token accounts of the wallet they touch are its USDC and MEW accounts. swapBuyUnshared is the SAME buy quote built with useSharedAccounts false: Jupiter answered with route_v2 (bb64facc31c4af14) and put the intermediate in the WALLET's wrapped-SOL account, created by a second idempotent create in the same transaction and never closed (no wrapping was asked, so nothing closes it) — the wallet would be left holding a wrapped-SOL account it did not have, its rent paid from the SOL that pays the fees. The check refuses that shape by name.
